1.q: בְּ⁠רֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ם בֶּן־יֹאושִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הָיָ֞ה הַ⁠דָּבָ֤ר הַ⁠זֶּה֙ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֔ה מֵ⁠אֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה
1.note: Jeremiah is using this statement to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **reign**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the time when Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, ruled]

The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly. This also occurs in verses 4, 9, 14, and 16.

2.q: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔⁠י עֲשֵׂ֣ה לְ⁠ךָ֔ מוֹסֵר֖וֹת וּ⁠מֹט֑וֹת וּ⁠נְתַתָּ֖⁠ם עַל־צַוָּארֶֽ⁠ךָ
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh said to me that I should make for myself bonds and yoke bars, and put them on my neck]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5. This also occurs in verses 4, 16, 19, and 21.

3.note: This event happened after Jeremiah made the bonds and yoke bars. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [And then send them]
Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean the people who are descended from Ammon. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the king of the Ammonites]
Here, **by the hand of** represents by means of. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by means of the messengers]

4.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֥ה תֹֽאמְר֖וּ אֶל־אֲדֹֽנֵי⁠כֶֽם
4.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says that you must tell your masters]
See how you translated the similar expression in 19:11.
See how you translated this name in 20:12. This also occurs in verse 18.

5.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I myself** separately, even though the verb translated as **made** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who made the earth and everything in it. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I am the one who made the earth]

The expressions **by my great strength** and **by my outstretched arm** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [by my very great power]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by being very strong]

Here, **my outstretched arm** represents the power with which Yahweh acts. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and by my great power]

Yahweh is using **in my eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in my judgment.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in my judgment]

Here, **the face of the earth** represents the surface of the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the surface of the earth]
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:6.

6.note: The phrase **And now** introduces what Yahweh is doing in the present situation. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [So at this time]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I myself** separately, even though the verb translated as **have given** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who has handed these lands over to Nebuchadnezzar. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I am the one who has given]

Yahweh is using the term **lands** to represent the people who live in those lands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the people of these lands]
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:7.

Yahweh says **also the living creatures of the field I have given to him** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [And I have given him such complete authority that it extends to the wild animals of the field]
In this verse, the word **animal** is singular in form, but it refers to all wild animals as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “animal” as in the UST.

7.note: Yahweh says **all the nations** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [And nations everywhere will serve him]

8.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific **nation** or a specific **kingdom**. He means nations and kingdoms in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [any nation or kingdom that will not serve him]

Yahweh is speaking of a nation that refuses to submit to the king of Babylon as if it were an ox that would **not put its neck in the yoke** of a farmer. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will not submit to the authority of the king of Babylon]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:12. This also occurs in verse 13.

Yahweh is referring to punishing that nation in a polite way by using the phrase **I will visit upon that nation**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [I will punish that nation]
See how you translated **the declaration of Yahweh** in 1:8. This also occurs in verses 8, 11, 15, and 22.
Here, **by his hand** represents by means of him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by means of him]

9.note: The pronoun **you** refers to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon, to whom Yahweh is sending this message. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And as for you kings]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. This also occurs in verse 14. Alternate translation: [saying that you will not have to serve the king of Babylon]

The pronoun **they** refers to the prophets, diviners, dreamers, soothsayers, and sorcerers mentioned earlier in the sentence. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [for your prophets, diviners, dreamers, soothsayers, and sorcerers are speaking to you]

10.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because they are prophesying falsehood to you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **falsehood**, you could express the same idea in another way. This also occurs in verses 14–16. Alternate translation: [falsely]

Here, **so as to** marks **remove you far away from on your land** as the goal or purpose of what the prophets are doing when they are **prophesying falsehood** to the people. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

11.q: וְ⁠הַ⁠גּ֗וֹי אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבִ֧יא אֶת־צַוָּאר֛⁠וֹ בְּ⁠עֹ֥ל מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וַֽ⁠עֲבָד֑⁠וֹ
11.note: Yahweh uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between a nation that refuses to serve the king of Babylon and a nation that submits to him. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [On the other hand, the nation that brings its neck into the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **nation**. He means nations in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But any nation that brings its neck]

Yahweh is speaking of a nation that submits to the king of Babylon as if it were an ox that **brings its neck into the yoke** of a farmer. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 12. Alternate translation: [submits to the rule of the king of Babylon]

12.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about whom Jeremiah spoke to after the verb **I spoke**. Alternate translation: [And I spoke to Zedekiah, king of Judah]

The phrase **all these words** refers to the message that Yahweh gave Jeremiah for the kings of the neighboring nations in the previous verses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [according to this same message that Yahweh had given me for the other kings]

The word translated as **live** is an imperative, but it communicates a good result rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a good result for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a good result. Alternate translation: [and serve him and his people, and if you do, you will live]

13.note: Jeremiah is using the question form to urge Zedekiah and his people to submit to the king of Babylon. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It is senseless for you and your people to die.]
The pronoun **you** refers to Zedekiah king of Judah, whom Jeremiah is addressing. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [you, King Zedekiah, and your people]

14.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 23:16. This also occurs in verse 16.

15.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because I have not sent them]

The pronoun **I** refers to Yahweh, whose words Jeremiah is reporting, while the pronoun **them** refers to the prophets who are speaking to the people. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, have not sent those prophets]

Here, Yahweh is saying **my name** to represent his authority. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [are prophesying with my authority untruthfully]

16.q: וְ⁠אֶל הַ⁠כֹּהֲנִים֩ וְ⁠אֶל כָּל הָ⁠עָ֨ם הַ⁠זֶּ֜ה דִּבַּ֣רְתִּי
16.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about whom Jeremiah spoke to after the verb **I spoke**. Alternate translation: [And I spoke to the priests and to all this people]

16.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֨ה כְלֵ֧י בֵית־יְהוָ֛ה מוּשָׁבִ֥ים מִ⁠בָּבֶ֖לָ⁠ה עַתָּ֣ה מְהֵרָ֑ה
16.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that the vessels of the house of Yahweh will soon be brought back from Babylon]

The expression **are being brought back** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Babylonians are returning the vessels of the house of Yahweh]

In this verse, the word **people** is singular in form, but it refers to all the people of Judah as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “people.” Alternate translation: [all these citizens]

17.note: Yahweh is using the question form to urge the priests and the people to serve the king of Babylon so that their city will not be destroyed. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [This city should not become a ruin!]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **ruin**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [completely ruined]

18.q: וְ⁠אִם־נְבִאִ֣ים הֵ֔ם וְ⁠אִם־יֵ֥שׁ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אִתָּ֑⁠ם יִפְגְּעוּ־נָא֙ בַּֽ⁠יהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לְ⁠בִלְתִּי־בֹ֜אוּ הַ⁠כֵּלִ֣ים הַ⁠נּוֹתָרִ֣ים בְּ⁠בֵית־יְהוָ֗ה וּ⁠בֵ֨ית מֶ֧לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֛ה וּ⁠בִ⁠ירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָ⁠ה
18.note: Yahweh is speaking of himself in third person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [And if they are prophets, and if my word is with them, let them please intercede with me, that the vessels remaining in my house and {in} the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem not go to Babylon]

Jeremiah is presenting a possible condition, that these men really are prophets and that Yahweh has actually given them a message. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [And if they really are prophets, and if Yahweh has truly given them a message]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:9.
Yahweh is speaking of the palace of the king of Judah as if it were a **house** in which he lived. Alternate translation: [the palace of the king of Judah]

19.q: אֶל־הָֽ⁠עַמֻּדִ֔ים וְ⁠עַל־הַ⁠יָּ֖ם וְ⁠עַל־הַ⁠מְּכֹנ֑וֹת וְ⁠עַל֙ & יֶ֣תֶר הַ⁠כֵּלִ֔ים
19.note: The implication is that these were valuable items made of bronze that were part of the temple. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [concerning the bronze pillars, and concerning the Sea, and concerning the bronze stands, and concerning the rest of the valuable bronze items]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:6.

20.q: אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־לְקָחָ֗⁠ם נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל בַּ֠⁠גְלוֹת⁠וֹ אֶת־יְכָונְיָ֨ה בֶן־יְהוֹיָקִ֧ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֛ה מִ⁠ירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶ֑לָ⁠ה וְ⁠אֵ֛ת כָּל־חֹרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִ⁠ירוּשָׁלִָֽם
20.note: Here Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

21.note: The expression **For thus says Yahweh of Armies** introduces a direct quotation that continues to the end of following verses. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [For this is what Yahweh, commander of the heavenly armies, says]

22.note: The expression **will be brought** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The Babylonians will carry them to Babylon]

Yahweh is using **the day of my visiting them** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the time when I turn my attention to them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the time when I act with regard to them]

The expressions **bring them up** and **restore them** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and I will surely bring them back]
